decisive_items: his cow had similar lesions on its teats
vesicles that ruptured and formed hemorrhagic crusts
Dermoscopy (10×) of one nodule showed an erythematous area with central ulceration and crust
response.rationale: Dairy farm exposure with cow teat lesions and vesiculocrusting nodules strongly indicate Paravaccinia (milker's nodule); Orf is typically from sheep/goats, and erysipeloid lacks this nodular crusting pattern.

rejected.why: Orf disease is usually associated with sheep/goats, not cattle; no direct support spans.
Orf virus infection misattributes cattle exposure; dermoscopy and cow lesions better fit Paravaccinia.
Erysipeloid presents as cellulitis-like erythema, not multiple crusted nodules with cow teat lesions.
Duplicate label of Paravaccinia without independent support; R5 is the specific and complete candidate.
